title: Reverse Nodes in Even Length Groups
description:
You are given the `head` of a non-empty singly linked list. The nodes are sequentially partitioned into contiguous groups whose target lengths are the natural numbers `1, 2, 3, 4, ...`. The final group may contain fewer nodes than its target length if the list ends early.

Reverse the nodes in every group whose **actual** length is **even**, and leave every group of odd actual length unchanged. Return the `head` of the modified list in `O(1)` extra space.
constraints: The number of nodes in the list is in the range [1, 10^4].
hints: For each group with target size `g`, first count how many nodes `actual` are actually available (at most `g`) before deciding whether to reverse.
If `actual % 2 == 0`, reverse exactly `actual` nodes starting from `prev.next` and update `prev` to the new tail of the group; otherwise simply advance `prev` by `actual` steps.

examples.explanation: Groups are [1] (len 1), [1, 0] (len 2, reversed -> [0, 1]), [6] (len 1, odd so unchanged).
Groups are [1] (len 1), [1, 0] (len 2, reversed -> [0, 1]), [6, 5] (len 2, actual length is even so reversed -> [5, 6]).
